text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Bill Clinton and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu affirm that they have reached results that will encourage the resumption of Syrian-Israeli peace talks.

- The ministerial committee for the development of tourism approves 11 touristic projects in the Red Sea with a total cost of 1.173 billion pounds ($345 million). Government will also transfer 18 plots of land owned by the army to the governorate. Construction permits for sites on the Mediterranean coast will not be given.

- Donor states show willingness to support Egypt's health services and give $1.5 billion. Health Minister Ismail Sallam says the draft proposal which Egypt submitted to the meetings of the World Bank and European Commission in Washington were met with great interest.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri meets tomorrow with 15 ministers to follow up the results of the Cairo economic summit.
- Proposed touristic projects in the Red Sea will provide 9,265 job opportunities.

- Al-Akhbar has gleaned that the state wants to increase the capital of one of the four main public sector banks and that it might even sell five percent of the bank's equity to Egyptians. The name of the bank has not been decided yet. The four main state-owned merchant banks are Banque Misr, Banque du Caire, Bank of Alexandria and the National Bank of Egypt.
- Widespread public and official condemnation of the events in Abu Qurqas. Ten Coptic Christians were killed when suspected Moslem militants sprayed a church with gunfire.
- Speaker of parliament Fathi Sorour inaugurates the Women's Forum in New Delhi.
- Transport and Communications Minister Soleiman Metwalli declares Arish port in Sinai a commerical port that will help export goods from all sectors of the economy.
